item2_route_from_step0.verdict: FlagGems dW really executes from the warmup on (whitelist matches == flag_gems.mm calls: 2640 / 2640 over 5 route processes; per process 0 in warmup step 0, 96 in warmup step 1, 432 in the hit step). At warmup step 0 (identical initial model, batches and RNG in every process) route-vs-native differs in 281-319 of 386 dense gradient tensors with max_abs at most 0.00195; native-vs-native differs in 289-320 with max_abs at most 0.00195: the same band. From warmup step 1 on, native-vs-native itself differs in 386/386 tensors (max_abs 0.26-2.3), so from-step-0 comparisons cannot isolate a route effect. per_step_state_hashes_diag.note: 6 processes (3 native, 3 route, --copy-grads none); hashes of the dense parameters and of the CUDA / CPU RNG states taken right after each step

item2_route_from_step0.note: the saved per-step gradients (~600 MB per process and step) stay on the measurement host; the JSON holds the per-pair comparisons

1_first_backward_is_not_bitwise_reproduc.design: 3 fresh processes, native path, one entry-loop step on batches 0-3, no host access to the gradients before clip; clipped gradients / parameters / optimizer state copied to the host after optimizer.step()

3_forward_is_a_deterministic_function_of.design: the state after step 0 of one process (parameters, optimizer state, CPU+CUDA RNG) is saved and loaded by 3 fresh processes; step-1 forward on batches 4-7

4_loss_is_extremely_sensitive_to_single_.design: same saved state, N random dense parameter elements moved by exactly one bf16 ulp before the step-1 forward
4_loss_is_extremely_sensitive_to_single_.mechanism: contrastive loss with temperature 0.05: logits = cosine / 0.05 are ~20x the embedding differences and are computed by an autocast bf16 matmul, so a 1-ulp change of ONE weight already moves the micro-batch loss by ~0.1%

why_trajectories_diverge_after_a_real_up.5_consequence: after one real update the processes differ in ~0.0007% of the parameters by 1 ulp, which through (4) gives ~1% differences in the step-1 loss and 10-50% differences in the later grad norms; the RNG states stay hash-identical. Trajectory-level comparisons between a candidate and native (from-step-0 runs) are therefore dominated by this amplification; same-state single-step comparisons (item 1) are the valid instrument.
why_trajectories_diverge_after_a_real_up.round57_correction: the round-57 statement that the native warmup is reproducible across fresh processes (5/5, sha b133cb9f...) referred to a 'warmup' WITHOUT optimizer updates (parameters unchanged) plus one update; with real updates the warmup state differs in every process (train_state_r58.json: 5 distinct snapshot hashes).

item3b_gemm_tiers.window: SINGLE-STEP window: the per-shape rows come from ONE training step (kernel_efficiency_r36, step 2). Every device_ms / headroom_ms in this block is per step-2 window; 772.12 ms is the 3-step mean backward-GEMM time and is a different window.
item3b_gemm_tiers.token_dim_rule: flattened-token dim = the operand dimension of [M,K,N] that is NOT a fixed model dimension (1024 / 4096): [4096,5120,1024] -> 5120 (K), [5120,1024,1024] -> 5120 (M), [1024,5120,1024] -> 5120 (K, was 1024 under the previous dX-takes-M rule). Rows with neither M nor K a model dimension are the loss matmuls (listed separately). Both model dims -> dW takes K, dX takes M. The old max(M,K) rule counted the fixed FFN feature dim 4096 as a long sequence (review BqpXfeg item 4).
item3b_gemm_tiers.regroup_note: round-58 (review 7182886976 item 3): the two [1024,5120,1024] rows move from the short tier to the long tier (5120 flattened tokens); the two loss matmuls ([40,10,1024] dW and [10,40,1024] dX) are listed separately. item3b_gemm_tiers.headroom_definition: device_ms - FLOPs/(139.2e12) per shape, summed over the tier, clamped >= 0: the ideal-device-time gap under the 139.2 TFLOP/s reference assumption; NOT an end-to-end ceiling
